subject: Agricultural Science
examFormat: Three papers (1, 2 and 3), all compulsory; Papers 1 and 2 are a composite paper taken at one sitting. Paper 1: fifty multiple-choice questions, 50 minutes, 50 marks. Paper 2: six essay questions, each drawn from at least two themes in the syllabus, answer five, 2 hours 10 minutes, 90 marks. Paper 3: practical paper for school candidates (alternative to practical paper for private candidates), four questions all to be answered, 1 1/2 hours, 60 marks.
excluded: Preamble (farm/school requirements, practical notebooks, visits) and examination scheme (summarised in examFormat). The syllabus has no country split, so everything else is included. The syllabus section letters (A-I) are not kept as topics; their numbered items are the topics. The Practical Agricultural Science section is included as topics prefixed 'Practical:'.

topics.name: Meaning and importance of agriculture
objectives: Define agricultural science and state its branches
State the importance of agriculture to the individual, community and nation

topics.name: Problems of agricultural development and possible solutions
objectives: Identify problems of agricultural development related to land tenure, basic amenities, finance, transportation, storage and processing facilities, agricultural education and extension, tools and machinery, farm inputs, marketing system and environmental degradation
Suggest possible solutions to the identified problems

topics.name: Subsistence and commercial agriculture
objectives: Explain the meaning of subsistence and commercial agriculture
Distinguish between subsistence and commercial agriculture based on their characteristics
State the advantages and disadvantages of subsistence and commercial agriculture
Identify the problems of subsistence and commercial agriculture
topics.content: Assessment would include incidence of pests and diseases, vagaries of weather, labour and government policy.

topics.name: Roles of government in agricultural development
objectives: Describe government agricultural finance: credit and subsidy
Describe the role of agricultural education
Describe agricultural extension services
Describe agricultural policies and programmes
topics.content: Assessment would cover past and present programmes, e.g. OFN, ADP, Farm Settlement, Agricultural Sector Rehabilitation Project (ASRP) and National Aids Coordination Secretariat.

topics.name: Role of non-governmental organizations in agricultural development
objectives: Explain the meaning of non-governmental organizations (NGOs)
State the roles of NGOs in agricultural development
topics.content: Examples of NGOs that would be assessed: West African Rice Development Association (WARDA), International Institute for Tropical Agriculture (IITA), International Livestock Centre for Africa (ILCA), International Crop Research Institute for Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT).

topics.name: Agricultural laws and reforms
objectives: Describe land tenure systems in West Africa
State government laws on land use in West Africa
State the advantages and disadvantages of the Land Use Act (Decree) and reforms in West Africa
topics.content: Assessment would include the Land Use Act (Decree) and land reforms in West Africa.

topics.name: Meaning and importance of agricultural ecology
objectives: Explain agricultural ecology and ecosystem
Identify the components of the farm ecosystem, e.g. biotic and abiotic
Describe the interactions of the components in the terrestrial and aquatic agro-ecosystem
topics.content: Interaction of farm crops/animals with other components of the ecosystem in farm settings, such as mono or sole cropping system, mixed cropping system, mixed farming system, fish ponds and forest (rain or savannah), would be assessed.

topics.name: Land and its uses
objectives: Explain the meaning of land
State the characteristics of land: free gift of nature, immobile, limited in supply etc.
State the agricultural uses of land: crop production, wildlife conservation/game reserve, livestock production etc.
State the non-agricultural uses of land: industry, housing, transport etc.
topics.content: Assessment would include uses of land for aquaculture, forestry and apiculture. Non-agricultural uses of land such as health centres, church/mosque, mining, recreational centres, schools and markets would be assessed.

topics.name: Factors affecting land availability for agricultural purpose
objectives: Identify physical factors: soil type, topography, land degradation, soil pollution
Identify economic factors: population pressure, expansion of industries, mining/mineral exploitation, recreation/tourism
Identify socio-cultural factors: land tenure system, religious purpose (church, mosque and shrine) etc.

topics.name: Agro-allied industries and relationship between agriculture and industry
objectives: Identify agro-based industries and raw materials: paper industry (pulp wood), beverage industry (cocoa, tea etc.), textile industry (cotton), soap industry (oil seeds etc.)
Explain the relationship between agriculture and industries: agriculture provides a market for industrial products, e.g. farm machinery and chemicals, and provides food for industrial workers
topics.content: Assessment would include other agro-based industries and raw materials, e.g. leather industry (hides and skin), canning industry (meat and fish), and other relationships between agriculture and industries.

topics.name: Environmental factors affecting crop and animal distribution and production
objectives: Describe climatic factors, e.g. rainfall, temperature, light, wind, relative humidity
Describe biotic factors, e.g. predators, parasites, soil micro-organisms, pests, pathogens and weeds, and interrelationships such as competition, parasitism and mutualism (symbiosis)
Describe edaphic factors: soil pH, soil texture, soil structure, soil type etc.

topics.name: Rock formation
objectives: Identify the types of rock: igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic
Describe the processes of rock formation
topics.content: Assessment would cover identification, description and examples of rock types, and how igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks are formed.

topics.name: Soil formation and profile development
objectives: State the factors of soil formation: the parent rock, organisms, climate, topography and time
Describe the processes of soil formation: physical weathering and chemical weathering
Describe soil profile development
topics.content: The role played by each factor in soil formation would be assessed. The meaning, importance, identification and description of each horizon of the soil profile would be assessed.

topics.name: Types, composition and properties of soil
objectives: Identify the types of soil
Describe the chemical and biological composition of soil: soil macro and micro nutrients, soil water, soil macro-organisms, soil microbes and soil air
Explain soil pH
Describe the physical properties of soil: soil texture and soil structure
topics.content: Assessment would cover types of soil and their separation into sand, silt and clay fractions, water holding capacity, porosity, capillarity, consistency etc. Determination of soil pH, and causes and correction of soil acidity/alkalinity, would be assessed.

topics.name: Plant nutrients and nutrient cycle
objectives: Identify macro and micro nutrients, their functions and deficiency symptoms in crops
State the factors affecting availability of nutrients in soil, such as pH, excess of other nutrients, leaching, crop removal, oxidation and burning
Describe methods of replenishing lost nutrients, e.g. crop rotation, organic manuring, fertilizer application, fallowing, liming, cover-cropping
Describe the nitrogen, carbon, water and phosphorus cycles
Explain the meaning and importance of organic agriculture
topics.content: Macro-nutrients such as N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S and micro-nutrients such as Zn, Fe, Mo, Co, B, Cu would be assessed. Types of fertilizers and methods of fertilizer application would be assessed. Assessment would include the description and importance of nitrogen, carbon and water cycles.

topics.name: Irrigation
objectives: Explain the meaning of irrigation system
Identify the types of irrigation systems: overhead (e.g. sprinkler), surface (flooding, furrow/channel, basin, border) and underground (perforated pipes, drips)
State the advantages and disadvantages of irrigation systems
State the importance of irrigation
Identify the problems associated with irrigation

topics.name: Drainage
objectives: Explain the meaning of drainage
State the importance of drainage
Identify the types of drainage systems: surface drainage (channel, furrow) and subsurface/underground drainage
State the advantages and disadvantages of drainage systems

topics.name: Agricultural pollution
objectives: Explain the meaning of agricultural pollution
Identify the causes/sources of pollution of agricultural lands and fish ponds: excessive application of agricultural chemicals, marine and oil spillage, livestock waste and dung disposal etc.
State the effects of land/pond pollution on farmers and agricultural productivity
topics.content: Ways of minimizing land/pond pollution would be assessed.

topics.name: Simple farm tools
objectives: Explain the meaning of simple farm tools
Identify the types of simple farm tools: cutlass, hoe, spade, shovel etc.
Describe general maintenance of simple farm tools
topics.content: Assessment would include identification, description and uses of each of the tools.

topics.name: Farm machinery and implements
objectives: Identify farm machinery: tractor, bulldozer, shellers, dryers, incubators, milking machines, combine harvester etc.
Identify tractor-coupled implements: ploughs, harrows, ridgers, planters, harvesters, sprayers etc.
topics.content: Assessment would include the meaning, uses/functions and identification of different parts of each of the farm machinery and implements. Engineering details are not required.

topics.name: Maintenance practices and precautionary measures
objectives: State the reasons for maintaining farm machines
Describe maintenance of farm machinery: check water and oil levels regularly, carry out routine service, keep machines clean etc.
topics.content: Assessment would include precautionary measures in the use of farm machinery.

topics.name: Agricultural mechanization
objectives: Explain the meaning of agricultural mechanization
Identify mechanized agricultural operations
State the advantages and disadvantages of agricultural mechanization
State the limitations of agricultural mechanization
topics.content: Mechanized agricultural operations such as ploughing, harrowing, planting, harvesting and milking would be assessed.

topics.name: Prospects of agricultural mechanization
objectives: Suggest ways of improving agricultural mechanization
topics.content: Possible ways of improving agricultural mechanization, such as developing less expensive machines and establishing agricultural engineering schools for personnel, would be assessed.

topics.name: Farm power
objectives: Identify the sources of farm power
State the advantages and disadvantages of different sources of farm power

topics.name: Farm surveying
objectives: Explain the meaning of farm surveying
Identify common survey equipment
State the uses of farm survey equipment
Describe maintenance of farm survey equipment
State the importance of farm surveying

topics.name: Farm planning
objectives: Explain the meaning of farm planning
State the factors to be considered in farm planning
State the importance of farm planning
topics.content: Engineering details are not required.

topics.name: Principles of farmstead planning
objectives: Explain the meaning of farmstead
State the importance of farmstead planning
State the factors to be considered in the design of a farmstead
Describe farmstead layout
topics.content: Assessment would cover site selection, location of structures and sketching of farm layout.

topics.name: Classification of crops
objectives: Classify crops based on their uses, e.g. cereals, pulses, roots and tubers, vegetables
Classify crops based on their life cycle, e.g. annual, biennial, perennial, ephemeral
Classify crops based on their morphology, e.g. monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous crops

topics.name: Husbandry of selected crops
objectives: Give the botanical and common names of the crop, its varieties/types, and its climatic and soil requirements
Describe land preparation, methods of propagation, planting date, seed rate, spacing, sowing depth and nursery requirements
Describe cultural practices: supplying, thinning, manuring and fertilizer requirement and application, weeding, pests and disease control
Describe harvesting, processing and storage of at least one representative crop from each crop grouping
topics.content: At least one representative crop from each grouping: cereals (maize, rice, guinea corn, millet); pulses/grain legumes (cowpea, soya bean, pigeon pea); roots and tubers (cassava, yam, potatoes); vegetables (tomatoes, onion, amaranthus, okro, cauliflower, spinach); fruits (citrus, banana, pineapple); beverages (cocoa, tea, coffee); spices (pepper, ginger); oils (groundnut, sheabutter, sunflower, oil palm); fibres (cotton, jute, sisal hemp); latex (rubber); others (sugar cane etc.). A general knowledge of husbandry of all the crops listed is presumed.

topics.name: Pasture and forage crops
objectives: Explain the meaning of pasture and forage crops
State the uses of forage crops
Identify the types of pasture
Identify common grasses and legumes used for grazing livestock
State the factors affecting the distribution and productivity of pasture
Describe the establishment of pasture
Describe management practices of pasture
topics.content: Assessment would include the botanical names and characteristics of common grasses and legumes used for grazing livestock.

topics.name: Crop improvement
objectives: State the aims of crop improvement
Describe methods/processes of crop improvement, e.g. introduction, selection, breeding
State Mendel's laws of inheritance
State the advantages and disadvantages of crop improvement
topics.content: Assessment would include the meaning of crop improvement and the definition of some genetic terms: characters or traits, chromosomes, genes, Mendel's 1st and 2nd laws.

topics.name: Forest management
objectives: Explain the meaning of forest and forestry
State the importance of forestry
State forest regulations
Describe forest management practices
State the implications of deforestation

topics.name: Agro-forestry practices in West Africa
objectives: Explain the meaning of agro-forestry
Describe agro-forestry practices: taungya system, alley cropping, ley farming etc.
topics.content: Common tree species suitable for agro-forestry practices would be assessed.

topics.name: Meaning and importance of ornamental plants
objectives: Explain the meaning of ornamental plants
State the importance of ornamental plants

topics.name: Common types of ornamental plants
objectives: Identify types of ornamental plants according to their uses: bedding plants (mostly flowering plants), hedging plants, lawn grasses etc.
Give examples of ornamental plants
topics.content: Assessment would cover identification of various types of ornamental plants. The common and botanical names would be assessed.

topics.name: Settings and location for planting ornamental plants
objectives: Identify settings and locations for planting ornamental plants

topics.name: Methods of cultivating ornamental plants
objectives: Describe cultivation by seed
Describe cultivation by vegetative propagation
topics.content: The importance of each method and examples of ornamental plants propagated through such method would be assessed.

topics.name: Maintenance of ornamental plants
objectives: Describe maintenance of ornamental plants
topics.content: Reasons for carrying out maintenance operations such as watering, mulching and pruning would be assessed.

topics.name: Diseases of crops
objectives: Explain the meaning of disease
State the general effects of diseases on crop production
State, for each disease, the causal organism, economic importance, mode of transmission, symptoms, prevention and control measures
topics.content: Diseases of the following crops: cereals (smut, rice blast, leaf rust etc.); legumes (cercospora leaf spot, rosette etc.); beverages (cocoa blackpod, swollen shoot, coffee leaf rust etc.); tubers (cassava mosaic, bacterial leaf blight etc.); fruits (citrus gummosis, dieback etc.); fibre (black arm/bacterial blight of cotton etc.); vegetables (root knot of tomato or okro, damping off, onion twister etc.); stored produce (mould etc.). Assessment would include at least two fungal, two viral, two bacterial and one nematode diseases of the crops chosen from the list.

topics.name: Pests of crops
objectives: Explain the meaning of pests
Classify pests into insect-pests and non-insect pests
Classify insect-pests based on mouth parts with examples: biting and chewing, piercing and sucking, boring
Describe the life cycle, economic importance, nature of damage, and preventive and control measures of important field and storage insect-pests of major crops
Identify non-insect pests, e.g. birds, rodents etc.
State the side effects of preventive and control methods: chemical (pollution, poisoning), biological (disruption of the ecosystem etc.), cultural (harmful effects of burning etc.)
State the general effects/economic importance of pests
topics.content: Major insect-pests: cereals (stem borer, army worm, ear worm etc.); legumes (pod borer, aphids, sucking bugs and leaf beetle); beverages (cocoa mirids/capsids); tubers (yam beetle, cassava mealybugs, green spider mites, variegated grasshopper); fibre (cotton stainer, bollworms); fruits and vegetables (thrips, grasshopper, leaf roller, leaf beetle, scale insect); stored produce (grain weevils, bean beetle). Nature of damage, economic importance, and preventive and control measures of each of the non-insect pests would be assessed.

topics.name: Weeds
objectives: Explain the meaning of weeds
Identify the types of weeds
State the effects of weeds on crops and the economy
State the characteristic features of weeds
Describe methods of controlling weeds: cultural, biological, chemical, physical and mechanical methods
topics.content: Common and botanical names would be assessed.

topics.name: Types and classification of farm animals
objectives: Identify types of farm animals: cattle, sheep, goat, poultry, pig, rabbit, fish etc.
Classify farm animals according to habitat (terrestrial and aquatic)
Classify farm animals according to uses (food, protection, pet etc.)

topics.name: Anatomy and physiology of farm animals
objectives: Identify the parts of farm animals
Identify organs of farm animals, e.g. heart, liver, lungs
Describe systems of farm animals, e.g. digestive system, circulatory system, respiratory system
topics.content: Drawing and labelling of parts of farm animals, and identification of important organs and their functions, would be assessed. Assessment would include the digestive system of poultry and differences between the monogastric and ruminant digestive systems.

topics.name: Animal reproduction
objectives: Explain the meaning of reproduction
State the roles of hormones in reproduction of farm animals
Describe the reproductive systems of farm animals
Describe the processes of reproduction in farm animals
Describe egg formation in poultry
topics.content: Assessment would include oestrus cycle, heat period, mating, gestation period, parturition, lactation, colostrum, mammary glands, signs of heat, ovulation etc.

topics.name: Environmental physiology
objectives: Explain the meaning of environmental physiology
Describe the effects of changes in temperature, relative humidity and light on growth, reproduction, milk production, egg production etc.

topics.name: Livestock management
objectives: Explain the meaning of livestock management
Describe requirements for livestock management (housing, feeding, hygiene and finishing) of at least one ruminant and one non-ruminant from birth to market weight
State the importance of management practices
topics.content: Assessment would include extensive, intensive and semi-intensive systems of management and record keeping in livestock management.

topics.name: Animal nutrition
objectives: Explain the meaning of animal nutrition
Classify feeds
State the sources and functions of feed nutrients
Identify types of ration/diet and their uses, the components of a balanced diet, and production and maintenance rations
State the causes and symptoms of malnutrition and their correction in farm animals
topics.content: The biochemical details of the nutrients are not required. Assessment would include the types of diet for the various classes of animals, their characteristics and supplementary feeding, and malnutrition-related conditions such as ketosis and rickets.

topics.name: Rangeland and pasture management
objectives: Explain the meaning and importance of rangeland/pasture to livestock and the characteristics of rangeland
Identify common grasses and legumes in rangeland
State the factors affecting the level of production of herbage: rainfall, grass/legume composition, grazing etc.
Describe methods of rangeland and pasture improvement: controlled stocking, rotational grazing, use of fertilizers, introduction of legumes, reseeding, weed control, burning, pest and disease control

topics.name: Animal improvement
objectives: Explain the meaning of animal improvement
State the aims of animal improvement
Describe methods of animal improvement: introduction, selection, breeding
Explain the meaning of artificial insemination
Describe methods of collecting semen
State the advantages and disadvantages of artificial insemination
topics.content: Assessment would include differences and similarities between breeds (local, exotic and cross/hybrid) and performance of animals.

topics.name: Animal health management
objectives: Explain the meaning of disease
Identify causal organisms: viruses, bacteria, fungi and protozoa
Identify factors that could predispose animals to diseases: health status of animals, nutrition, management etc.
Explain the reaction of animals to diseases: susceptibility and resistance
Describe the causal organisms, symptoms, mode of transmission, effects, prevention and control of selected livestock diseases
Explain the meaning and types of parasites
Describe the mode of transmission, life cycle, economic importance and control of selected livestock parasites
Describe general methods of prevention and control of diseases and parasites: quarantine, inoculation/immunization, hygiene, breeding for resistance etc.
topics.content: Selected livestock diseases: viral (foot and mouth, rinderpest, Newcastle); bacterial (anthrax, brucellosis, tuberculosis); fungal (aspergillosis, ringworm, scabies); protozoa (trypanosomiasis, coccidiosis). Selected parasites: endoparasites (tapeworm, liverfluke, roundworm); ectoparasites (ticks, lice). The economic importance of the diseases would be assessed.

topics.name: Aquaculture
objectives: Explain the meaning of aquaculture
Identify types of aquaculture: fish farming, shrimp farming, crab farming
Explain the meaning and importance of fish farming
State the conditions necessary for siting a fish pond
Describe establishment and maintenance of a fish pond
Explain fishery regulations
Describe fishing methods and tools
topics.content: Assessment would include aeration, stocking, feeding, harvesting, processing and preservation of fish.

topics.name: Apiculture or bee keeping
objectives: Explain the meaning of apiculture or bee keeping
Identify types of bees: indigenous and exotic
State the importance of bee keeping
Describe methods of bee keeping: traditional and modern
Identify bee keeping equipment: bee hives, hive tools such as suits, smokers, jungle boots, brushes etc.
State precautionary measures in bee keeping, e.g. locate apiaries far from human dwellings, put warning symbols near the apiary

topics.name: Basic economic principles
objectives: Explain scarcity
Explain choice
Explain scale of preference
State the law of diminishing returns

topics.name: Factors of production
objectives: Describe land, capital and labour (characteristics and classification) as factors of production
Describe management or entrepreneur as a factor of production
topics.content: Rural-urban migration and how it affects labour availability in agricultural production would be assessed.

topics.name: Principles of demand
objectives: Define demand
State the law of demand
State the factors affecting demand for agricultural produce
Explain movements along the demand curve
Explain shifts in the demand curve

topics.name: Principles of supply
objectives: Define supply
State the law of supply
Explain movements along the supply curve
Explain shifts in the supply curve
State the factors affecting the supply of agricultural produce

topics.name: Implications of demand and supply for agricultural production
objectives: Explain price support
Explain price control
Explain subsidy programmes and their effects on agricultural production

topics.name: Functions of a farm manager
objectives: Explain the meaning of a farm manager
State the functions of a farm manager
topics.content: Assessment would include the meaning of farm management.

topics.name: Problems faced by farm managers
objectives: Identify the problems faced by farm managers

topics.name: Agricultural finance
objectives: Explain the meaning of agricultural finance
State the importance of agricultural finance
Identify sources of farm finance
Classify farm credit by length of time (short-term, medium-term, long-term), by source (institutional, non-institutional) and by liquidity (loan in cash, loan in kind)
State the problems faced by farmers in procuring agricultural credit, e.g. high interest rate, lack or inadequate collateral
State the problems faced by institutions in granting loans to farmers, e.g. lack of records and accounts
Explain the meaning of capital market and the institutions that deal with medium and long term loans for agricultural business
Identify sources of funds for the capital market: bonds, insurance companies, merchant banks, the stock exchange
State the roles of capital markets in agricultural business: mobilization of long term funds for on-lending, reducing over-reliance on the money market etc.
topics.content: Assessment would include the meaning of agri-business.

topics.name: Farm records and accounts
objectives: State the importance of farm records
Identify types of farm records: inventory, production, income and expenditure, and supplementary or special records
Design farm records
Describe farm accounts: expenditure/purchases account, income/sales account, profit and loss account, balance sheet
topics.content: Assessment would include terms such as salvage value, appreciation, farm budget, depreciation and inventory, their importance and their uses in calculating profit and loss of farm items like crops, livestock, farm machinery and tools.

topics.name: Marketing of agricultural produce
objectives: Explain the meaning and importance of marketing of agricultural produce
Identify marketing agents and their functions
Describe marketing functions: assembling, transportation, processing etc.
Describe marketing of export crops
Identify export crops in West Africa
State guidelines for exporting crops in West Africa
Identify corporate bodies, cooperative societies and individuals engaged in exporting agricultural produce, e.g. ANCE (Association of Nigerian Cooperative Exporters)
State the importance of exporting agricultural produce
Identify problems of marketing agricultural produce
topics.content: Advantages and disadvantages of the marketing agents would be assessed.

topics.name: Agricultural insurance
objectives: Explain the meaning of agricultural insurance
State the importance of agricultural insurance

Identify types of insurance policies: specific enterprise insurance (crop, livestock), farm vehicle insurance, fire disaster insurance (machines and buildings), life assurance (farmers, farm workers and farmers' household)
Explain insurance premium
Identify problems of agricultural insurance: uncertainties of weather, losses due to natural disaster etc.

topics.name: Agricultural extension
objectives: Explain the meaning and importance of agricultural extension
Describe agricultural extension methods: individual contact methods, group contact methods etc.
Identify agricultural extension programmes in West Africa, e.g. ADP, NDE, Agro-service centres, state ministries of agriculture and natural resources
Identify problems of agricultural extension in West Africa, e.g. illiteracy among farmers, inadequate transport facilities
topics.content: Qualities of a good extension worker would be assessed.

topics.name: Practical: Soil
objectives: Examine soil samples for texture by manual feeling of wet and dry soil
Examine fertile and infertile soils and note distinguishing features: colour, texture and structure, presence of organic matter and living things

topics.name: Practical: Soil profile
objectives: Describe and identify a soil profile

topics.name: Practical: Rocks
objectives: Identify common rock types: igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic

topics.name: Practical: Laboratory work on physical properties of soil
objectives: Carry out mechanical analysis by sedimentation and by the hydrometer method or sieves
Determine bulk density and total pore space
Determine moisture content of a moist soil sample
Determine maximum water holding capacity
Determine wilting point
Determine capillary action

topics.name: Practical: Laboratory work on chemical properties of soil
objectives: Determine soil acidity using a pH meter and/or other simple equipment
Identify common types of chemical fertilizers (nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and compound fertilizers) and their methods and rates of application
Identify organic manures: green manure, farm yard manure and compost, and their method of preparation and application

topics.name: Practical: Irrigation and drainage
objectives: Identify and state the uses of irrigation and drainage equipment, e.g. watering can, sprinkler, pump, pipes

topics.name: Practical: Farm tools and equipment
objectives: Identify, describe, use and maintain garden tools and equipment, e.g. hoe, cutlass, garden trowel, hand fork, shovel, spade, rake, sickle, secateurs, shears, long handle hoe, pruner, budding knife, emasculator

topics.name: Practical: Tractor and animal drawn implements
objectives: Identify, describe, use and maintain tractor and animal-drawn implements, e.g. ploughs, harrows, ridgers, planters, cultivators
Identify the major parts of the implements and their functions

topics.name: Practical: Harvesting, processing and storage equipment
objectives: Identify, describe and state the uses of harvesting, processing and storage equipment, e.g. dehuskers, shellers, winnowers, dryers, processors, graters, refrigerators, cutlasses, scythe, groundnut lifters

topics.name: Practical: Farm tractor
objectives: Identify the major components of the farm tractor
Carry out servicing and maintenance of the tractor

topics.name: Practical: Uses and maintenance of horticultural tools and implements
objectives: Identify, use and maintain horticultural tools: shears, dibber, pruning knife, secateurs, budding knife, measuring tapes, hand fork, hand trowel, hoe, fork

topics.name: Practical: Livestock and fishing equipment
objectives: Identify, describe, use and care for livestock and fishing equipment, e.g. waterers, feeders, milking machines, nets, hook and line, branding machine, egg candler

topics.name: Practical: Farm surveying equipment
objectives: Identify, use and care for simple surveying equipment, e.g. measuring tape, pins or arrows, ranging poles, plumb bob, offset staff, compass, Gunter's chains, pegs, theodolite

topics.name: Practical: Seeds, seedlings, fruits and storage organs of crops
objectives: Identify seeds, seedlings, fruits, storage organs and essential parts of the common crop plants, pasture grasses and legumes

topics.name: Practical: Main pests and diseases of crops
objectives: Identify and control the main field and storage pests, e.g. cotton stainer, yam beetles, weevils, and the damage they cause to crops
Identify the main diseases of crops, their causal agents and characteristic symptoms, and their prevention and control

topics.name: Practical: Planting dates, seed rates, plant population and seed quality tests
objectives: Determine planting dates, seed rates, plant population and seed quality tests of the more common local crop plants

topics.name: Practical: Seedbed preparation and crop husbandry operations
objectives: Prepare seedbeds
Carry out fertilizer application, mulching, use of pesticides, watering, vegetative propagation, germination tests etc.

topics.name: Practical: Forest products and by-products
objectives: Identify forest products and by-products

topics.name: Practical: Methods of propagation of horticultural plants
objectives: Carry out propagation methods: direct sowing, transplanting, layering, grafting and budding

topics.name: Practical: Common weeds
objectives: Identify the external features of common weeds
State their mode of dispersal and methods of controlling weeds on the farm

topics.name: Practical: Common breeds and types of animals
objectives: Identify common breeds of animals and types of animals available in the locality
Restrain, handle and groom farm animals

topics.name: Practical: Major internal organs of farm animals
objectives: Identify the major internal organs of farm animals, e.g. organs of the digestive, reproductive and excretory systems, and their functions

topics.name: Practical: Animal by-products
objectives: Identify animal by-products, e.g. hides and skin, fur, feather, horn

topics.name: Practical: Animal feeds and feed stuffs
objectives: Identify animal feeds and feed stuffs and their local sources, and state their uses, e.g. fish meal, groundnut cake, rice bran
Identify types of diets/rations

topics.name: Practical: Main pests and parasites of farm animals
objectives: Identify common ectoparasites (e.g. ticks, lice) and endoparasites (e.g. tapeworms, liver flukes, roundworms)
State the damage caused on their hosts, their control and their life cycles

topics.name: Practical: Diseases of farm animals
objectives: Describe methods of prevention and control of diseases of farm animals, e.g. drugging, drenching, dipping, spraying and simple methods of farm sanitation

topics.name: Practical: Routine management practices in farm animals
objectives: Carry out routine management practices, e.g. selection of livestock and poultry for breeding, culling, ear-notching, tattooing, horn or skin branding, debeaking, dehorning, castration
Identify the equipment/tools used for routine management practices

topics.name: Practical: Fish harvesting and preservation
objectives: Describe methods of harvesting, processing and preservation of fish
